# Review finding: ownership-unaware cleanup of shared keyed state (P0)

Repo: claude-baseline-R1-isolated-1 (workspace associations). File: cleanup.py:3. Date: 2026-10-11.

Pattern: a "simplification" changed a failure-cleanup path to delete a shared, workspace-keyed record (`store.active.pop(workspace_id)`) without checking that the failing job owns it (`active[workspace_id]["setup_id"] == setup_id`). When queued cleanup runs after a different setup has completed (an ordering the README explicitly allows), it silently deletes the newer job's association.

Detection heuristic: cleanup/rollback/compensation code that deletes by a shared key (workspace, tenant, user) instead of by the job's own ID, or without a compare-and-delete on an owner field. Usually goes along with tests that only cover cleanup by the current owner.

Fix: guard with an owner check (compare-and-delete); add a regression test where a stale job's cleanup runs after a newer job completes.
